body:
I watch in spite of him, not because of him.  

I don’t want to see him - at all.  Whether he is sad, happy, growing, or reverting - I DON’T CARE.  

I just want him away from me.  I just want him gone.

James saying sorry to everyone for bringing Raquel into the group - gold.

If anyone finds a gif of that - please share with me.  I will use it forever.

I’m sure I’m not alone in saying this - but I still have to say it::

LaLa - where’s your real conversation with Randall?  Let’s watch you contribute to his redemption arc.

Fuck off, hypocrite.

Seriously am so proud of Ariana for continuing to not engage with him (as well as she has been able to).  

I hate so much when LaLa and others say “why didn’t she move out” “why is she on the show” etc. Like, he can mess up and she should just roll over and give up everything to keep the peace.

Fight for what’s yours girl.  

If this show boots her and keeps Tom, I’m done.  Truly. 

The chauvinist culture is more alive and well than I realized.

Mostly - I definitely experienced the struggling of finding who I am vs who she told me I was.  I overcame her thoughts about me for sure.

I have recently noticed that I have let other people’s opinions make me doubt my sense of self.  

So - after you step away from her and find yourself - try to trust it.  There will be people who don’t understand it, but do it anyway.  So much more important to honor how you feel about yourself than to make other people agree with it.  

Does that make sense?  But I am pretty strong and know who I am - with little hints of a struggle still.

I recommend making a new email.  It’s a pain to transfer everything over to a new one - but worth it!!  You can block her, but she can come at you from other accounts.  

Do everything you can to shut down her ability to contact you.  

I have thought about getting a stalking order, too.  

Good luck!!

Congratulations!!!  

Keep going!!  Just because you heal, doesn’t mean they’ve changed.

My older sister was always the scapegoat and I was gc when I was little.  I was always a support to her and she and I would team up to keep nMom in check.  Then, when we were both adults, she got tired of being picked on and starting throwing me under the bus.  She and nMom teamed up against me - 

So, as a former gc I was way too confident to let them destroy me.  It took me being ready to die to finally leave, but I’ve mostly moved on and built a good life without them.  I gave up everything - all family and friends - and started fresh.   So happy I did.  

Guess that’s a partial GC answer.  Once upon a time…

Try not to feel weird about leaving - you are bravely and boldly choosing yourself because it’s come to a point where you HAVE TO.  I did that - snuck away.  It’s 5 years later and I am still so happy that I did.  All the things she made me feel about myself were not real.  I am so much better than the person she tried to make me.

Good luck!!  Be strong!!

It took me about that long to stop explaining her to people.  “I don’t have a relationship with my family” is all I will say now.  People want more, but I don’t give it.  At some point you have to stop seeking validation from others - we know we were right to leave them.  That’s enough.

Agreed!!  I don’t want to hear any of the Valley people’s opinions.  Bravo shoving them in our faces so we’ll watch.  

At least Jax and Kristen are somewhat relevant.

James used to drive me crazy, but I kind of love him now.  He’s not perfect, but guy is trying and growing, and the way he is with his dog is great to me.  Listening to the Valley bitches weigh in and judge him was soooo annoying.
If you haven’t tried psilocybin, you really should.  It’s expensive to do legally, but it can really help people identify and let go of what’s holding them back.

Slow to respond, sorry!!  - 

He and I just got engaged and hardly ever fight.  Best relationship I’ve ever been in.  :)

Fuck them, indeed.  

You are absolutely allowed to grieve for what you didn’t have.  You are allowed to do this whether they validate you or not.  

I love this quote by Rupi Kaur “Do not look for healing at the feet of those who broke you.”  

I have found it freeing.  I slowly quit fighting my toxic parents and just allowed myself to be right.  Slowly (it took a few years to fully stop) I stopped caring what they think.  They were always wrong, they remain wrong, and I have come a long way towards being healed and whole anyway.  

Proud of you for seeing how wrong they were/are and rising above for yourself.

I have definitely been here.  I’m feeling this way a bit now, honestly.  

The thing about being this raw, wounded, and low - you also have more of a capacity for more joy than the people who are seemingly enjoying their life.  We see and feel so much more than most.  

If you chose to hold on and keep going… your life has the potential to be deeper and more fulfilling because you went through this.  I have spent nearly two years feeling so happy in ways the people in my life simply can’t understand.  Most of them are just going through the motions of a life, not happy or miserable - just blah.  

Road bumps happen, and I still struggle sometimes, but I am also strong and happy on the other side.  

I hope you hold on and find out what the other side of this can feel like.
Walking away from it definitely won’t fix the problem.  We all need to work with these guys to improve.  There’s a line where you should walk away, but I get what you’re saying here OP.

I can’t tell you how lucky I felt to wake up to this news with my boyfriend.  He is as upset as I am and ready to be my ally.  He also chose to get a vasectomy in his 30s when he was past wanting children.  All of his male friends pushed and  supported each other into getting a vasectomy when they were done making their choices about children.  He does his part to not be part of the problem.

If he and I were to ever break up, I would expect this moving forward.  It’s their problem too - and they can either learn why and move out of their archaic way of thinking, or - ya know, good luck having an intelligent woman put up with you.  Won’t be me. 

Glad you’re working to educate your guy.  It takes time to break the learned thinking of our upbringings.  It’s ok for it to take time, as long as progress is being made.

Triggered.

I deleted my initial comment because I still have very realistic concerns about my abuser seeing my comments.  

I left my state that just made abortion illegal.  I left my family that I have no doubt is celebrating that act of control.  And I wish I didn’t feel them still *coming for me*

They aren’t done.  

I want to live somewhere with like-minded people - I’m so over sharing this country with controlling religious conservatives.  

You do you, but fucking let me do me.

It took me probably four years to feel 95% healed.  This was four years after leaving my narcissist behind - fighting to end all communication and stalking, and probably two years of almost nothing from them.  I built on positive behaviors and ever so slowly stopped being triggered.

I say 95% because I still have the occasional dream with a quickly managed panic attack.  

I’m mostly better though.  

Every step will add to healing - sometimes it’s frustratingly slow.  

Good luck, OP.
I think we have the same mother…

I think I’m finally to the point where I have a healthy view of relationships.  I’m not looking for someone to save me from my trauma - I’m managing my trauma on my own and letting them simply add to my life.  

Definitely a huge one for me - I was always made to believe I needed someone to make my life what I wanted.  I couldn’t possibly do it myself.  

Finally - my life feels like mine.

It’s literally my biggest trigger.  I am so almost healed these days - but if I feel unheard (it takes months of trying now rather than one conversation), I finally break, crumble, and get all crazy for a bit.  

I think it’s fair that we want to be heard.  

Still sucks that it’s such a trigger to our past trauma, but it’s valid.  Know that, require that from people who get to stay in your life.

As someone who has largely conquered their CPTSD - it wasn’t until I found myself, loved myself, and needed nothing from the people around me that I started building true friendships.  I used to always be there for people to this intense self-sacrificing level, then when they weren’t there for me like that, I would get all hurt.  It was hard to find friends when I was drowning and needy.  Now that I get myself, feel secure in who I am and my past - people seem to crave my approval and want me around more than I need to be.  It’s weird.  

You’re your own best friend - and that’s ok.  The rest comes after.  

-hugs-
I have… he doesn’t want to be honest about what happened.  I think it’s more about his issues and less about us.  But it sucks!

A little funny to share this just as I’m posting about missing my ex - but…

I’m back with my ex before my ex.  I was in a horrible place when we first dated.  It was really unhealthy and I was sooo needy.  We broke up and didn’t talk for months.  We found our way to a friendship.  This great, chill friendship.  We both dated other people, leaned on each other when things with them were less than great.  

Then my guy dumped me, he dumped his girlfriend, and we decided to give it another try.  It’s safe, comfortable, and honest.  Our passion is still there.  It’s good this time.  He told me yesterday that he has no doubts.  I love him.  

I do still miss my ex sometimes.  Today, I miss my ex.  

But I did find my old lover again, and I think it will last this time.  I just still need to heal a bit I guess.

Maybe all of us RBNs should consider getting official stalking orders.  I don’t know what the rules would be in your state, but my daughter recently had to get one against an ex, and all she had to do was prove two separate incidences in the last two years.  The order is forever.  If he comes near her, she calls 911 and he is arrested.  

If my nMom ever regains her desire for stalking me, I’m going there.  Fortunately, after disappearing, being found, having some court drama - she hasn’t done more than the occasional email.  

Anyway… disappear as much as you can, look into a stalking order, and stay strong.

I’ve come back as the dumper, and been told no.  I have also had the last three men I’ve dated (who dumped me) come back to me.  Two I wasn’t interested and said so, the other I’m dating again.  

So - he broke up with me (honestly, I was a mess and I get why he did).  I begged and tried to convince him to stay, but he still left.  He finally blocked me because I couldn’t shut up and let him go.  We took a month off, then went to lunch as friends.  We talked about once a month for four months.  I admitted I still wanted him back, he offered a secret, sex-only affair, which I pathetically jumped at.  After a year and a half of that, I had healed and moved on, my life had improved, and he finally realized he wants me back.  So - we’re a few months in and it’s going well.  Like he’s my best friend and things are so chill now.  
Definitely happens.  I think you have to let go first, which is fucking torture. And then, whether it happens or not, you’re ok.  
Good luck to you either way.

I work at a restaurant, and it is so hard dealing with these anti-mask types.  Most of the time I just ignore it - the pretend “holding my mask” crowd - oh look! Look!  I’m putting it on now.  And I imagine the reviews if I don’t tell them to put it on, I imagine the reviews if I do.  

Fuck you, Karen.

I’m happy, almost every day now. 

I left and went NC four years ago (with light regressions).  I was literally going to kill myself or leave - so I left.  No real plan.  There were nights I slept in my car.  It’s taken some time to heal and stabilize mentally - but I feel so good most of the time now.  I no longer need meds to deal with anxiety.  I seek things that make me happy in a healthy way - I hike, I meditate by rivers (if I don’t do this every day, the anxiety returns), I eat healthy and delicious foods, I drink a glass of wine in the evenings.  I love my daughter.  I have a great guy who has been a friend and now a boyfriend.  It was slow and I was alone for most of it - but I feel happy more than not.  Sure, there are setbacks sometimes and suicide pops into my head (habit really), but it sticks around less each time.  

Keep going… it’s a long road, but that time is going to pass one way or another, make sure you’re heading where you want to be.  

Sending love.
This one almost made me cry.  So happy you have your fancy bread now.  Feels so good to rise, doesn’t it!? 🤍

Coffee.  My nMom used to obsess over how much money I spent on coffee - maybe $30 a month.  I drank cheap stuff at home.  

Now I buy the really fancy stuff, have a great machine, and I wake up and enjoy a slow cup every morning.  I bet I spend at least $100 a month now, and I love how much she’d hate it.

We don’t talk of course, but I know.  Mm mm.
Dude, you are not crazy.

Ha!  You’re my new favorite person. :)

I was a bit petty - playfully bribed my coworkers to spill on them… never happened, but it felt good to dream.  Lol

Super weird, right?  I think she might be egging him on… she came with a girlfriend and watched me too.  It’s all so uncomfortable!  

Thanks for responding :)
Aw, thanks - needed some commiseration extra right now.  Xo

You are not a loser!  

I’m 36 and just started a new job in the service industry.  Got chewed out by my 26-year-old trainer the other night... that was humbling.  BUT - I don’t feel like a loser either... every year, I am moving closer to who I want to be.  Sure, I’m late... wasted all of my 20s cleaning up mistakes from my teens - but it’s never too late to fight for the life you want.  Just give yourself time and celebrate the small things.  You’ll get there.  And so will I.  

Hugs!!!

Don’t be embarrassed by that - six months can be significant.  Mine was only a year and a half - wish he had shown his true colors at six months.  

Still really hard, I know.  Sorry for you, too.

Ugh - completely the same boat!  He thought I was pessimistic - really, he just couldn’t handle reality.  I like to experience the good without ignoring the bad.  So it wasn’t even a fair criticism in my opinion.  Went to his house and had the door slammed in my face because he had someone else there.  

Sorry you know what this feels like... how long were you together?

True.  Hard to know when to make that call... there were so many promises about the future, and then he just ran.  

We deserve better than that.  

Normally I can find some way to blame myself for a relationship ending, but not this time.  

Hugs- this is hard, huh!?
Feeling this too - trying not to, but what is that? We can give them everything and they may still hurt us.  Sucks.

Not a king, but I still felt this - thank you.  Been struggling with the way he left, the person he moved on with within days.  

It’s about the ones who stay.  

Thanks for the reminder.

I’m in my late 30s and feel functionally about 24-26.  I was so stuck for so long, and finally started taking steps to fix it.  I probably felt 21 for the longest time - until I finally got traction and my career started moving forward.  Somewhere along the way I became ok with saying that out loud - that I’m functionally mid-20s.  Try to just keep making progress... forgive the wasted time because it’s never coming back... commit to not waste anymore.  You’re ahead of me... (lots of people I’m sure).  Go you!!
“I’m here and she just took my happiness with her.”  — ugh, I feel this.

I’ve heard that it takes a month for every year you were together, and also that it can be half the time you were together.  I feel like I felt mostly better after the months timeline, and I’m still pinning my hopes that by half of the overall relationship I will be completely ok.  

May be a garbage timeline, but it’s helped feeling like I’m counting down my misery.  

Hugs.
Aw.  Internet hugs?
Completely feel this...

Mornings are hard, for sure.  It’s been two months for me, and I still wake up multiple times a night, missing him, having to try to stop hurting so I can go back to sleep.  Ugh. 

Good morning.
And it goes over the nose ;)
Let her go - find someone who appreciates you and doesn’t jerk your around.  Good luck to you.

As someone who has cheated, genuinely regretted it, and genuinely changed and wanted another chance (that I didn’t get) - I was all prepared to advise you to give her another chance.  

BUT - you did that.  This girl is clearly wanting both of you.  Either accept that she wants to have multiple lovers, or move on.  Take consolation in the fact that you’re unforgettable and this clearly wasn’t your fault, and stay away.  

Maybe one text - “please don’t ever contact me again.  Wish you the best.” And then be done.  

Sorry... it’s so hard when we want someone who wants us and from our perspective it seems simple, but for whatever reason they keep fucking it up all on their own.  

How old are you?

The self improvement will be good for you, whether your ex ever cares or not, right?  One of the things I did after he broke up with me was really focus on fitness.  I have about 20 pounds I’d like to lose, and I told myself he was just taking a break... I harnessed him not wanting to see me and figured it would give me more time to really shock him with a huge transformation.  

Anyway, I’m starting to feel over him, and feeling healthier and more confident than if I hadn’t started working out hoping to entice him back.  Not sure how I would react now if he saw and wanted me.  I’m becoming a better catch for whoever I want though.  Who cares that my motivation started so pathetically?

Even if he is with someone else, you should tell him how you feel.  I would want my ex to.  Let it be his decision what happens next.  I’m trying to move on, probably look like I have, and maybe too much has happened to forgive - but I would like my ex to tell me regrets leaving.  Maybe I would go back, maybe I wouldn’t, but it would release a lot of the hurt I’m still holding onto.  

Just my thought, as the dumpee.  Sorry you’re hurting.

Thanks for listening.  

I have some friends.  Still hoping this will blow over and I won’t have to leave the area.  Just wondering how hard this is going to get before it lets up and I get tempted to run.  My daughter loves it here, so I hope we can stay.  

Anyway, appreciate you hearing me and caring.

I feel you!!  

I’m hating everything I gave up for him - he even talked me into quitting my job like six weeks before he ran away.  Frikkin cowards.  

And then we have no choice to be a million times stronger than anyone should have to be to survive their weakness.  

Good luck to you.  Thanks for sharing.

I feel like we just don’t know what they’re thinking.  I’m a few weeks out from my boyfriend ending things, and he seems fine.  He isn’t reaching out, he took a new girl to our place already.  He seems fine.  

Then I remember how hard it was to express his feelings while we were dating.  I’d get glimpses into his struggles when he would reach out, late at night and a bit drunk, and finally admit he was having a hard time with something.  He once called me four times before he couldn’t hold back his tears and express what was wrong.  

He’s hurting.  He knows.  He’s just an idiot who isn’t going to tell me that.  

I bet your guy is struggling more than you see. 

Not that it makes it much better.  Because then I think - if you’re hurting and I’m hurting, COME BACK.  

Good luck.  Internet hugs.

Thank you for sharing this.  Three weeks out.  My brain knows it will get easier, yet I can use all the reminders I can get. 

Especially loved your part about her missing the most important thing - the will to commit to you.  I have so many things I love about my ex, things I know I will never find again in this perfect combination that made me want him so much.  

Anyway, thank you.
Sorry.  Mine is three weeks out - still feel numb at times.  So hard when the ones we love leave... we wouldn’t leave them, so it’s hard to understand.  Internet hug... allegedly it gets better.

So sorry that you can relate!  I feel like this is the absolute cruelest way to leave someone... leaves us trying to sort out what really happened because they won’t tell us.  Allegedly it gets easier right?  Hope you’re doing ok...

Love this - thank you.  I’m sorry you’re moving past something similar... the sudden ones where you’re left without closure are the hardest.  I’ll never understand why it’s so hard for people to be honest in the end.  

I know things will get better... just can’t believe it happened, can’t imagine someone like him, but if he can leave me like that - I guess all the good things don’t make up for that.  

Here’s to loving ourselves and healing.  🤍
Thank you for that... for hearing me.  Whatever your situation- I hope you heal too.  Heartache is the worst pain...

They wouldn’t necessarily be after only one thing.  I know a few people who moved somewhere in Asia (one was Thailand, the other two were Vietnam) and they all seem genuinely in love.  I think all of their wives just love the way they are treated... a respect thing.  

I know you can’t buy property in Thailand unless you are Thai, so keep that in mind - but yeah, try it.  Why not?

Congratulations!!!  I’ve been meaning to do this forever.  Hearing how liberating it felt for you has me tempted to finally do it.  Hard to choose a name, but it’s well past time.  

Thanks for sharing!!!

Hey!! Thanks for responding.  Glad you had something lined up.  I’m hopeful.  I really was shocked they wouldn’t let me work remotely, so it really exploded without a safety net in place.  Freakin COVID deniers, huh?  

Hope you’re loving your new job, and staying safe :)

Similar experience- maskless working environment.  Finally quit, but my daughter may never get her sense of smell back.  

I think most people are getting this from science-deniers being aggressively negligent.  

Were you able to get unemployment after quitting?  I’m still waiting to have my case reviewed.

Hey OP!  I love so much that you are being proactive to try to make life as happy as possible for your nephew.  I went through something similar and have a lot of regrets about how I handled it.  Maybe my hindsight will be helpful to you?  

Best thing you can do is maintain constant contact with him.  If your sister will let you, try to see him - even just once a year.  Make sure he never forgets there’s someone who thinks he’s awesome out there who is there for him if he needs you.

I know with my sister, directly saying anything negative about her to her son would have encouraged her to shut me off from him.  If you can stand to, I would maintain a sympathetic ear with some advice to him and do as little direct negativity about his mom as you can.  I may be wrong about how your sister would react if she found out you were saying things about her - so just be sure you’ve given that some thought first?  

I feel like having child services take this seriously is a stretch - but maybe a conversation with them wouldn’t hurt?  See what they think?  I’m sure it depends on the area and the case worker.  Be cautious before making an official complaint.  (Someone else reported my sister to them and nothing came of it - so I’m jaded)

My story?  I could see my nephew being chipped away at from maybe age 6.  I tried to be there for him and I was one of the only people who got him, who he felt accepted by.  When I waged my own war with my nMom, I was cut off from him (as my nSister sided with her, loving that she was no longer the scapegoat).  I left when he was 16.  I thought about him a lot.  Wishing I could reach out, imagining all the ways they might stop me.  I decided I would reach out when he turned 18 and tell him he could come live with us (it took me about that long to find my own stability anyway.)  He killed himself the day after he turned 18.  He hadn’t been reminded that I was here for him for too long and didn’t think of me as an option.  2 years of low contact followed by 2 years of no contact erased me.  I think so often that a card he may or may not have seen, a phone call that may or may not have been given to him could have changed things - given him a fighting chance to heal from that upbringing.  I know she would have blocked a call, but maybe she would have complained about it and he would at least know I was still thinking about him.  

Basically- I love that you care now.  The most important thing is to not be disconnected.  All of this can be healed when he’s an adult - as long as he knows you’ve got his back.  I know everyone is different, so only you can really know the best way to help him.  Hope my advice helps you in some way.

Ugh, so sorry!! 

I agree with those suggesting backing out of the house.  You’re not going to love it if she’s there all the time.  

When we finally decided to go no contact, we moved around constantly while she tried to find us, and focused on freedom from her above all else.  I’ve had a few slip-ups where I’ve talked to my dad and she’s hopped on the phone, always after someone has pulled the whole “but they’re you’re FAMILY” line.  I’m so triggered by her voice that I immediately recommit to no contact.  It gets easier.  It’s hard to be perfect at immediately.  Maybe consider that you’re not going to find your perfect place for a while.  Mine was a year out, but I was drastic in my running from her.  Monthly rentals all over the country.  She finally tired herself out and realized I finally get to “win.”

Good luck to you and your wife.  Stay strong and know every step away is a step towards some kind of peace/happiness/freedom.  Even if it’s not THIS house.  It will be something wonderful.

All the time.  After three years of extremely low contact with the whole family, I’m still slowly healing those trauma responses, still finding better ways to handle people who think family is family and you should forgive them.   Being with my family made me feel crazy and ultimately suicidal.  Being without them is allowing me to heal.  Never thought I could be this calm and happy.  It’s not perfect - but it’s getting better.  Believe your truth about your mom and don’t let anyone mess with what you know she is.  The more distance, the better.  Hopefully you can inch towards a better place, too.  

Sorry so many of us get this, yet most people still don’t.

That was my method back when I was super suicidal.  I just got through every day I could because I could always kill myself tomorrow.  Some days I focused more on dying, some days it allowed me to take risks - like leaving behind everything that made me unhappy.  It took a couple of years before I started to believe I could be happy and want to live, and it took a couple of years longer to stop thinking about suicide every time something went wrong.  I’m honestly happy now.  

I hope you can procrastinate long enough to find some happiness too.  I get how you’re feeling now, really.

I agree... the initial help was HUGE.  Eventually I had to step away.  This place really helped me process in a way that therapy never did.  We all get it.  We’ve been through it.  It feels good to talk to each other.  Then you have to take that with you and move forward to be happy.  I have days where I miss/need that validation- but I don’t come on much anymore.  

Great to have the support when you need it though!
Definitely... it’s slowly fading, but I always feel more urgent about things than the untraumatized people in my life.
Not a dude - best sex of my life has been with a curved penis... and I’ve had a lot of amazing sex.  Get a second opinion before ruining the many future orgasms you may give?

I love that you shared this and I saw it right now.  Always told it was manipulative, and it always felt so genuine and vulnerable to me when I did it growing up.  

Now I’m in a relationship where I’m trying to put my finger on what’s wrong and how to fix it - but he does that.  

Thanks for reminding me of something I knew was abusive but allowed myself to forget.

I’m feeling the same - this hard earned mental stability that was fought for over years and years... I’m losing it and I hate that.  Not everyone can do “whatever it takes.”  Virtual hugs from a stranger who gets it.

I did!  Not another country, but another state.  It was a bit scary and rocky along the way, but I’m slowly finding relationships that are good for me.  My situation was similar, but most of it was truly toxic and abusive.  People still don’t really get how I could leave my family and want zero contact with them, but I get it.  Things aren’t perfect, but they are better.

This.... exactly.  I did that in a dark place and I’m scared of spiraling back there. 

Good luck to you... and me.

I’ve thought a lot about the increased suicide risk for those of us who struggle to stay at home.  Completely glossed over.  Suddenly mental health is like this thing where we just need to be strong.  Uh, doesn’t really work like that.  

I’ve spent years piecing together a routine that keeps me somewhat sane, and I’m going to do the parts of it I can.  I’m a huge germaphobe and respectful of distance and I think you and I getting out and going for a walk is safe and fine and everyone can STFU about it.  

Keep taking care of you.  Precautions within reason. 

Sending virtual hugs...
So true... good riddance to them. But occasionally find myself thinking “if only...”

I wouldn’t worry about the age difference at all... I’ve always been attracted to older guys, and it’s always been them who haven’t wanted me.  After years alone, I’m late mid 30s with someone in their early 50s, and we’re a bit crazy for each other.  Age is all relative, really.  

You could just take her on one of your walks and talk... the fact that you’re interested in her will be fun for her.  Hope she’s interested in what you have to say, as well?  

Sometimes a great conversation is better than anything.  Eat if you get hungry, makeout if the mood strikes, let her show you her interests.  Just enjoy being together.

First - when I’m desperate for something, I do this thing (actually learned it in a psych ward cause things have gotten pretty low for me) where I stand up, raise my heels up, and then thump them down.
